subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II report & secure transfer options
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II report & secure transfer options

Claire —

Hope you’re well. We’re in the final stages of procurement for our collaboration with Stratus Health and need to complete a security review before finance signs off. Could you share your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering the latest 12‑month audit period) and any accompanying bridge letter if the period doesn’t overlap our expected window?

To make this low friction, we can accept one of the following:
- Direct download link to a redacted report (drive or secure share)
- S3 presigned URL (we’ll provide a short-lived bucket)
- Secure SFTP drop (details below)

Quick asks to speed review:
- Audit period covered (start — end)
- Auditor name and report date
- Whether the report includes user‑access/SSO and logging controls (scoping summary is fine)

We’ve attached a short one‑page checklist (soc2-request-quick-ask.pdf) that lists minimal artifacts we look for. If you prefer, Marissa can share a short bridge wording we often accept for cases where the audit window doesn’t fully align.

If helpful, our team can coordinate a secure upload window on Friday (US PST). Please let us know which transfer method works and an approximate ETA.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: soc2-request-quick-ask.pdf
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stratushealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II report & secure transfer options

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the note and the checklist. We can absolutely help. A couple of clarifying Qs before we share: 

1) Audit period: Our latest Type II covers 2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30. Is that acceptable, or do you need coverage beyond Sep 30, 2026?

2) Bridge letter: We can provide a short bridge letter from our auditor, but we’d like to confirm the exact phrasing you need (extent of representation and which controls). Is a generic bridge referencing continuity of controls sufficient, or do you need statements tied to specific control categories?

3) Transfer method: We prefer SFTP (our security team wants to avoid public presigned URLs). We can also provision a secure share link if you give a drive folder.

We’ll need an LOA or a short access confirmation for the SFTP transfer (our security requires recipient details). Can you confirm the account name and who will download?

I’ll loop in security@stratushealth.com if we move forward.

— Claire Huang
Head of Vendor Programs | Stratus Health
claire.huang@stratushealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II report & secure transfer options

Claire —

Thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the audit period. The 2025-10-01 — 2026-09-30 window is generally fine for our procurement baseline. If finance flags any gap we’ll request a bridge letter limited to continuity of controls through our signature date (simple affirmation of no material control changes since the report period).

In case it’s helpful, I’m attaching two short items we use internally: a sample bridge letter wording (bridge-sample.docx) and a set of short reply snippets you can drop into procurement/legal responses (reply-snippets.txt). We’re intentionally minimal — procurement primarily needs: (a) report PDF, (b) auditor name & date, (c) high-level scoping (whether IAM/SSO and logging are in scope), and (d) confirmation of secure transfer method.

Minimal artifact suggestions beyond the report (if available):
- Scoping matrix or page showing which trust services criteria were included
- Auditor contact name and report signature date
- Sample system logs (one week, redacted usernames) or log-retention policy excerpt
- SSO/IdP metadata or confirmation that SSO controls were assessed
- Evidence manifest (simple CSV) listing files being delivered

For SFTP LOA: if you share the downloader account name and intended transfer window we’ll confirm authorization and provide our SFTP endpoint details. If SFTP is cumbersome, we can accept an encrypted drive share link (we’ll provide recipient emails).

Thanks again. If you’d like a short call to finalize transfer, Rafael and I are available 10–11am PST tomorrow.

— Marissa Cole
Manager, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: bridge-sample.docx; reply-snippets.txt
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@stratushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 31 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II report & secure transfer options

Claire —

Appreciate the quick coordination. We’ll proceed as follows:

1) Transfer method: SFTP is fine — please send the LOA and we’ll provide the account name (redwood-soc2-ingest@redwood-sftp) and a 48‑hour window for the upload. Our security ops will rotate credentials after the transfer.

2) Deliverables we’ll accept (minimum): report PDF (redacted PII OK), auditor letter/date, scoping page, and an evidence manifest (CSV preferred). If you can include a one‑week sample of system logs (redacted) that speeds verification but is optional.

3) Bridge letter: If finance asks for a bridge, Marissa’s sample wording should be acceptable — short continuity statement referencing no material changes to controls since 2026-09-30. We don’t need control‑by‑control attestations for this path.

4) Timelines: would you be able to upload by EOD Monday, Jan 4? If not, reply with earliest ETA and we’ll adjust procurement deadlines.

I’ve attached a quick transfer how‑to (s3-presigned-instructions.txt) and an evidence manifest template (evidence-manifest.csv) to make the share straightforward. Once uploaded, please confirm the filename(s) in your reply and security@stratushealth.com can confirm receipt.

If any redlines are needed to the bridge wording, loop in your auditor and Marissa and we’ll move quickly.

Thanks again — looking forward to closing this out.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
